title: Yosemite National Park Trip Planner Printable, Yosemite Itinerary, Half Dome Permit Guide, Best Day Hikes, California Travel PDF
description:
Planning a first trip to Yosemite National Park? This 30-page printable guide puts the whole trip on paper: when to go for waterfalls, high country or quiet, how entry, passes and permits work, where to stay and when bookings open, and how to spend 1, 3 or 5 days.

WHAT'S INSIDE
- The park at a glance: Yosemite Valley, Glacier Point, Tuolumne Meadows, the Mariposa Grove, Wawona and Hetch Hetchy, and which base fits your trip
- When to go, month by month: waterfall season, when Tioga and Glacier Point roads usually open and close, crowds, fall color and winter
- Entry and passes: 2026 fees, annual passes, the non-resident fee, and what to check before booking a 2027 trip
- Getting there and getting around: the five entrances, free shuttles, regional buses and valley parking
- Where to stay and when to book: park lodging, gateway towns, campground release dates and a booking calendar you fill in
- Half Dome and wilderness permits explained simply
- Safety: rivers and waterfalls, storms on domes, heat, altitude, wildfire smoke, bears and food storage
- 16 day hikes sorted by effort, from Lower Yosemite Fall and Cook's Meadow to the Mist Trail, Sentinel Dome, Taft Point, the Grizzly Giant and Cathedral Lakes, with distance in mi and km and climb in ft and m, from NPS figures
- Big days for fit hikers: Half Dome, Upper Yosemite Fall, Chilnualna Falls, the Four Mile and Panorama trails
- Sample 1-day, 3-day and 5-day plans, packing checklist by season, trip budget, day-by-day planner and hike log

WHAT YOU GET
- US Letter and A4 versions
- Mobile edition, sized for reading on your phone
- Color and printer-friendly (low ink) versions
- Instant download. This is a digital file; nothing is shipped.
- Bonus: our free one-page Ultimate Hiking Checklist

GOOD TO KNOW
Checked against nps.gov in November 2026. Yosemite changes its entry rules, road openings, fees and permits from year to year, so check the official park website for your dates before you book. No maps or GPS files. Not affiliated with the National Park Service. For personal use.

Made by HikeSupply Co., a small shop for weekend hikers. More printable hiking guides in our Etsy shop.
